captions.threads:
Most people don't actually read their subscription terms until they need to cancel. That's the trap.

1/4 Here's what kills me: refund windows, billing cycles, and guarantee conditions shift between offers. What you bought three months ago might have different terms than what's being sold today. The company isn't necessarily being slippery, but they're not exactly making it obvious either. You have to know what to look for.

2/4 Before you hit that cancel button, you need three pieces of information. When does your current billing period end. What's the actual refund window for your specific offer, not the general policy. And what does the guarantee actually cover. Most people skip this and then wonder why they're out of pocket.

3/4 The difference between a clean cancellation and a messy one comes down to timing and documentation. Screenshot your terms. Know your dates. Contact support before the refund window closes, not after. This isn't paranoia, it's the difference between getting your money back and explaining to your bank why you're disputing it.

4/4 You deserve clarity on what you bought and what it costs to stop. If a company makes that hard, that tells you something about how they operate. The real win is knowing exactly where you stand before you need to make a decision.

entries.postTitle: Outgrowing Old Identities

captions.threads:
nobody warns you that the identity that got you here might be the exact thing holding you back now. i spent years perfecting this version of myself, optimizing for it, building everything around it. then one day it just... didn't fit anymore.

like wearing the same shirt for a decade. it was comfortable. it worked. people knew me in it. but my shoulders changed shape. my chest expanded. the sleeves started pulling weird.

the weird part? shedding it felt like losing something real even though it was always just a costume i put on every morning. there's grief in outgrowing yourself. there's also relief.

if you've ever felt that misalignment where your outsides don't match your insides anymore, where the strategies that built you aren't building you forward, that's not a failure. that's momentum asking for an upgrade.

2/4 The misalignment whispers before it screams. It shows up as restlessness you can't name. As projects that should excite you but feel hollow.
